label: March 1915
headline: Przemyśl Surrenders
deck: The Galician fortress falls to Russia; the fleet fails at the Narrows
caption: Austro-Hungarian prisoners march out of Przemyśl past Russian sentries
body: On 22 March the fortress of Przemyśl, in Galicia, surrenders to the Russian army. Besieged since November, its garrison of some 120,000 men has eaten its last horses. Before giving up, the defenders blow up their forts, guns and bridges.

All winter the Austro-Hungarian armies have attacked through the deep snow of the Carpathians to relieve the fortress. Whole units froze in the passes; now the Russians press into the mountains, and behind them lies the plain of Hungary.

At the Dardanelles, on 18 March, an Anglo-French fleet tries to force the Narrows by day. A line of mines laid in a bay the minesweepers had missed sinks the French battleship Bouvet and the British Irresistible and Ocean. The fleet withdraws; the straits must now be taken by troops.
In France the British take the village of Neuve Chapelle on 10 March, but the advance stalls within days.
briefs: The German cruiser Dresden is scuttled off the Juan Fernández Islands
Zeppelins bomb Paris on the night of 20 to 21 March
Britain extends its blockade to all goods bound to or from Germany
